messages:

Subject: Performance SLOs & Autoscaling follow-up

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the call today — great to learn more about FastPay's real-time fraud scoring use case. Per our discussion I wanted to recap the SLO / autoscaling constraints so we can align on next steps. Please confirm anything I've mis-captured.

Key SLOs and requirements (as discussed):
- Latency: P95 <= 120ms for single-turn scoring (non-streaming). For streaming scenarios (incremental scoring), need token-level streaming with first-token latency <= 80ms.
- Throughput / concurrency: steady-state 250 qps, peak bursts up to 1,200 qps for ~3–4 minutes during end-of-day batches.
- Concurrency per model instance: expected 8 concurrent scoring requests per GPU in your current infra mix.
- Scale-up / burst behavior: need burst capacity to cover the 1,200 qps peaks. Preferred approach is a warm pool that keeps 30% of burst capacity pre-warmed; scale-up target from cold to ready ~90s (hard requirement: <120s).
- Queueing / backpressure: acceptable queuing up to 30s for non-critical requests; critical scoring requests should not be queued beyond 10s — fallback to a lighter model or 429 preferred.
- Reliability: fallback model for graceful degradation; automatic routing to Dedicated region if hosted capacity constrained.

Attachments I've included: redwood-autoscale-design.pdf (high-level design), FastPay-SLO-requirements.xlsx (SLO checklist & sample traffic profile).

Proposed next steps:
1) FastPay shares 48 hours of representative traffic (anonymized) + 1 customer example where you expect peak behavior.
2) Redwood runs a scoped perf test against a dev endpoint with the target model and returns a throughput/latency profile.
3) We iterate on warm-pool sizing and cost estimates — Marcus will scope options (reserved vs. burst).
4) Plan a follow-up demo where Marcus shows autoscale behavior and tracing for a simulated peak.

Can you confirm steps 1–3 and share the sample traffic? Happy to set a time for the demo next week.

Thanks,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — this is a great recap and looks accurate. A couple quick clarifications:

- The 1,200 qps peak is sustained for about 3–4 minutes but can spike to 1,600 qps for under a minute during certain batch rollouts. Is the warm-pool approach comfortable handling that short spike?
- For streaming: when you say token-level streaming, do you have an expected bytes-per-chunk or time threshold (we're using a 50ms granularity at the moment).
- Cost: can you give ballpark monthly estimates for keeping 30% warm pool vs. relying on fast scale-up from cold?

We can share a sanitized traffic dump (JSON) tomorrow. Priya is looping in on infra sizing.

— Alex

Subject: Re: Performance SLOs & Autoscaling follow-up

Alex —

Answers inline below and next steps: 

- Short spikes to 1,600 qps: warm pool + short-term burst allocation handles these far more predictably. If you expect these sub-minute spikes regularly, we recommend sizing warm pool to cover ~50% of the typical burst and rely on a fast ramp for the remainder — that keeps steady-state cost lower while smoothing extreme spikes.
- Streaming granularity: our runtime supports 50ms chunks; first-token streaming latency target (<=80ms) is achievable with the token write buffer configured to flush every 40–50ms. We'll include specific buffer settings in the perf test runbook.
- Cost delta (ballpark): keeping 30% warm for your current profile is roughly +12–18% monthly infrastructure compared to purely cold starts with fast ramp. Exact figure depends on instance type and reserved capacity discounts — Marcus will provide estimates after he maps your sample traffic to instance profiles.

Next steps / owners:
- FastPay: share sanitized traffic (Priya) — owner: FastPay, ETA: Tue EOD.
- Redwood: perf test & warm-pool sweep (Marcus) — owner: Marcus Lin, ETA: Fri.
- Redwood: provide preliminary cost delta and warm-pool sizing options (Marcus + Rachel) — ETA: Mon next week.

I've linked the test runbook and added the SLO sheet to the Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-fastpay-autoscale
I'll set a demo for next Wed unless you prefer earlier.

Best,
Marissa

Subject: Re: Performance SLOs & Autoscaling follow-up — perf test plan

Alex / team —

I'll own the perf test for FastPay. Quick notes so expectations are clear:

- Test plan: 1) baseline single-instance latency profile (P50/P95/P99), 2) concurrency sweep (1–16 concurrent per instance), 3) burst simulation (ramp to 1.6x peak for 60s), 4) warm-pool reheating & cold-start ramp (measure ready times).
- Telemetry: we'll collect per-token latency, queue times, and trace IDs so you can map user-visible latency to infra events.
- Warm pool sizing: I'll run a cost sweep at 0%, 15%, 30%, and 50% warm-pool levels and output expected infra cost delta.
- Safe defaults: if any critical requests exceed 10s queue, we'll exercise fallback routing to lighter-model variant (configurable).

Please upload the sanitized traffic to the Drive link Marissa posted and ping me here when it's ready. I'll provision a short-lived dev endpoint and share endpoints + post-test logs.

Thanks — Marcus
